basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Floor Door Stoppers (Third Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Builder's Hardware (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Builder's Hardware Sectional Committee, CED 15, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, and finish of floor door stoppers used for holding doors open at a specific position.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Manufacturers are encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on bodies and packaging boxes. Compliance with IS 1823 is widely required in Central Public Works Department (CPWD) civil works specifications, military engineer services (MES) tenders, and commercial building construction contracts across India.

requirements.detail: Body and tongue shall be manufactured of cast brass, pressure die-cast aluminium alloy, or zinc alloy, fitted with a high-durability hard rubber or plastic cushion at the extreme end to absorb physical shocks.
All floor door stoppers in a consignment of the same shape, size, and manufactured from similar materials under identical conditions are grouped together to constitute a lot.
The number of stoppers to be randomly selected from a lot for inspection depends on the size of the lot, as prescribed in columns 1 and 2 of Table 4.

All selected sample stoppers are physically checked for dimensions, materials, manufacture, and surface finish. A stopper failing to satisfy any of these requirements is considered a defective stopper.

A lot is deemed conforming to standard requirements if the number of defective stoppers found in the sample does not exceed the permissible defective count given in column 3 of Table 4; otherwise, the lot is rejected.
Observed or calculated analytical values, physical dimensions, and clearances must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960 to match the significant places of the specified limits.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1823 : 1980 (Third Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification prescribing requirements for floor door stoppers. Maintained under the Builder's Hardware Sectional Committee (CED 15) and reaffirmed in 2022, the standard regulates materials, physical dimensions, manufacture, and finish for floor-mounted hardware. It unifies the types of metals permitted (such as cast brass or die-cast aluminium), requires an elastic rubber cushion at the tip to absorb impact shocks, and outlines randomized quality-control sampling plans in Appendix A. Consignments are inspected in lots of identical types and sizes; the entire lot is accepted or rejected based on a strict limit of allowable defective stoppers in the sample, ensuring reliable performance in commercial and residential buildings.
